[by Claude Code] ## Motivation In every GLM-5.2 decoder layer, the attention output and the MLP output (an MoE in 75 of the 78 layers) are each summed across the tensor-parallel ranks (an all-reduce), added to the residual and normalized (RMSNorm). All-reduce fusion runs these three steps as one kernel. On one Blackwell node at TP4, SGLang turns it on by itself with `--flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend auto`, which resolves to FlashInfer's `mnnvl` backend (MNNVL is multi-node NVLink; these kernels exchange data over the NVLink fabric). That fusion covers batches of up to 2048 tokens; larger prefill chunks fall back to an NCCL all-reduce and a separate RMSNorm. The opt-in `cutedsl` backend uses FlashInfer kernels written in CuTe DSL (CUTLASS's Python kernel language) over the same fabric. It fuses batches up to `--max-prefill-tokens` (8192 in this deployment) and, for batches of up to 192 tokens, also folds in the MoE finalize (the weighted sum of the selected experts' outputs) and the shared-expert add. This PR adds a Configuration Tips bullet to the GLM-5.2 cookbook that recommends `cutedsl` for one deployment: GB300 NVFP4, aggregated TP4, concurrency 1 (c1), a point of the page's Agentic Long-Context section. That section lists commands measured with AgentX, SemiAnalysis InferenceX's agentic-coding benchmark, which replays recorded multi-turn coding-agent sessions against the server. The bullet gives the measured effect, the builds the flag needs (those with #45565, which raised the default prefill CUDA-graph size for MLA models from 2048 tokens to min(8192, chunked-prefill size)), the limit of the evidence to c1, and a memory note. Defaults and runtime code do not change; the default stays `auto` because only this one deployment was measured. The PR also corrects the server-arguments row for this flag, which does not list `cutedsl` and says `auto` picks `mnnvl` on SM90 (the code picks `trtllm`). Impact: - **Decode (measured):** time per output token about 3.4% lower in three runs: −3.45% [95% CI −3.65, −3.18] (default vs default +0.04%), −3.41% [−3.59, −3.16] in a replicate, and −3.47% [−3.84, −2.99] in a shorter third run. GLM-5.2 NVFP4, one GB300 node, TP4, c1, AgentX replay, 148 paired requests. - **TTFT (measured):** not worse. p90 −3.94% [95% CI −16.55, +4.43] and −4.63% [−16.22, −0.68] in the two 1,200-s runs, and +2.49% [−11.17, +67.82], within its noise, in the 900-s third run; p50 not worse in any run. - **Throughput (measured):** +1.45% input + output tokens/s per GPU against the mean of the two default arms (replicate +1.38%). - **Accuracy (measured):** GPQA-Diamond 0.9116 → 0.9003, −1.14 points [95% CI −2.78, +0.51], no significant change; MTP accept length 2.729 → 2.742. - **Scope (measured):** c1 only. In a GB300 microbenchmark over 4–256 tokens per call, the CuTe DSL kernel was faster than `mnnvl` only at 4–12 tokens, and 1.05–1.13× slower at 16–20 and 1.05–1.10× slower at 96–256 tokens, so the bullet tells readers to re-measure before raising concurrency. - **Builds without #45565 (measured):** on `nightly-dev-20261016-a93f16f0` the flag raised p50 TTFT by 9.0% (decode still −3.24%), so the bullet names a minimum build. - **Memory (measured):** with the flag, PyTorch's caching allocator held about 8 GiB more idle cache per GPU while serving at `--mem-fraction-static 0.83`, leaving 0.45 GiB free for allocations outside PyTorch; emptying the cache brought both backends to the same level (within 0.8 GiB). No request failed. ## Modifications **+3 / −2 docs (2 files); no runtime code, no tests.** Base: `main` at `f2d31889258d22214d9541e40b1e1e6961ce95e7`. - **GLM-5.2 Configuration Tips** (`docs/cookbook/autoregressive/GLM/GLM-5.2.mdx`): one new bullet. It says what the flag changes and where it was measured, gives the effect, names the build requirement (#45565; the image the Agentic Long-Context section lists for this point, `nightly-dev-20261021-c1c287a4`, predates it), the older-build counter-example, the c1-only scope with the microbenchmark caveat and the memory note, and says that the Deploy panel cells do not set the flag. The bullet names `nightly-dev-20261026-8252e3af` (measured) or newer; the first nightly built after #45565 merged, `nightly-dev-20261024-5994c559`, was not measured. - **Server-arguments row** (`docs/docs/advanced_features/server_arguments.mdx`, `--flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend`): the description follows the field's help string on `main` and adds facts read from the code: when SGLang turns the fusion on by itself (including the DeepSeek-V4.1 TP4 exception), the 2048-token limit of `trtllm` and `mnnvl`, and for `cutedsl` its TP sizes, forward modes and workspace bound, and that it turns the other fusion off for the whole process, so speculative draft layers run unfused. The options column gains `cutedsl`. The old row's "Defaults to auto" and "mnnvl on SM90" did not match the code (`auto` picks `trtllm` on SM90).
Where each fact in the row comes from (code on main) - Help string: `python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/fields/exec_.py`; the options match the field's `Literal`, and the default stays `None`. - Auto-enable: TP size above 1, no DP attention, no MoE all-to-all backend, multi-node only on Blackwell, and not for DeepSeek-V4.1 (hidden size 5120) at TP4 on one Blackwell node, which keeps its custom all-reduce (`_flashinfer_allreduce_fusion_auto_enable` and `prefer_custom_dsv41` in `arg_groups/overrides.py`). - `auto` resolves to `mnnvl` on Blackwell and `trtllm` on SM90 single-node (`_resolve_backend` in `layers/flashinfer_comm_fusion.py`). - The 2048-token limit of the `trtllm` and `mnnvl` fusion: `FUSE_ALLREDUCE_MAX_BATCH_SIZE` in `layers/layer_boundary/residual/add_norm.py`. - `cutedsl`: TP sizes 2, 4, 8 and 16 (`SUPPORTED_TP_SIZES` in `layers/flashinfer_mnnvl_cutedsl.py`); decode, extend and target-verify batches only (`_is_supported_forward_mode` in `layers/layer_boundary/fusions/cutedsl.py`); workspace bound, the largest of `--max-prefill-tokens`, `--max-running-requests`, the CUDA graph batch sizes and the decode graph batch size × draft tokens (`_resolve_max_m`, `cutedsl_moe_max_num_tokens`); the other fusion is off for the whole process (`uses_cutedsl_ar_fusion`), and draft layers never get the CuTe DSL fusion (`install_cutedsl_fusion` returns `None` in speculative scope), so they run unfused.
- **Not changed:** the AgentX panel data (`docs/src/snippets/agentx/zai-org/glm-5.2.jsx`) and the Deploy panel. Each AgentX entry mirrors an InferenceX submission and links to the run that measured it. The GB300 Agg TP4 entry's run used `nightly-dev-20261021-c1c287a4` (before #45565) without this flag, so editing that entry here would attach a command to a run that did not measure it. The flag can enter that entry through the regular AgentX sync once an InferenceX run with it exists. **Checks.** - [x] `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args_docs_coverage.py` (the CPU CI test for `server_arguments.mdx`): 4 of 4 pass with this row on a CPU checkout of `main` at `cb55d77d`, and a misspelled flag in the new row makes `test_no_stale_rows` fail, so the test does read the row. Since then, `main` has changed none of the code this row describes (`exec_.py`, `overrides.py` and the fusion files have no all-reduce-fusion changes up to the base commit); CI reruns the test on this base. - [x] The pre-commit hooks that apply to `.mdx` files: no trailing whitespace, final newlines present, no merge markers, `codespell` clean on the added lines. The full `pre-commit run` was not completed locally. - [ ] `mint validate` and `mint broken-links` in `docs/` ## Accuracy Tests **GPQA-Diamond (measured).** `sgl-eval` 0.1.3 (the version pinned in `python/pyproject.toml`): 198 questions × 4 repeats, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95 (the checkpoint's recommended sampling), max tokens 200,000, 32 client threads. Real MTP acceptance (no simulation). Server: the launch command under Speed Tests without the `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_*` variables, plus `--max-running-requests 32 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 32` so that the 32 threads run concurrently. The two arms differ only in the flag. Build: the replicate build described under Speed Tests (Builds). The two arms ran on different GB300 nodes on different days. | | default (`auto` → `mnnvl`) | `cutedsl` | |---|---|---| | GPQA-Diamond pass@1 (792 samples) | 0.9116 | 0.9003 | | Paired difference per question (bootstrap, 10,000 draws) | | −1.14 points, 95% CI [−2.78, +0.51] | | MTP accept length (server counters) | 2.7293 | 2.7420 (+0.47%) | | Truncated responses | 0.13% | 0.38% | | Mean completion tokens | 23,542 | 23,951 | The interval contains 0, so there is no significant change. At this sample size a drop of about 2.3 points is detectable with 80% power, so a loss of about 1 point cannot be excluded.
GPQA command and dataset ```bash sgl-eval run gpqa --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 --model nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \ --n-repeats 4 --num-threads 32 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --max-tokens 200000 \ --chat-template-kwarg enable_thinking=true --from-dataset gpqa_diamond_public.jsonl ``` The Hugging Face GPQA set is gated, so both arms read the same local file: the 198 GPQA-Diamond questions from the public OpenAI simple-evals CSV, formatted with sgl-eval's own GPQA prompt formatting (seed 42) and passed with `--from-dataset`. Absolute scores may therefore differ slightly from runs on sgl-eval's own copy; the comparison is paired.
Precision (code reading of SGLang 8252e3af and FlashInfer 0.7.2, plus server logs) - No dtype or quantization change. The two CuTe DSL kernels SGLang calls (all-reduce + residual + RMSNorm, and MoE finalize + all-reduce + residual + RMSNorm) read and write BF16 and accumulate in FP32; neither has an FP8 or FP4 output. - One narrow change. In a `cutedsl` process SGLang turns off its older MNNVL all-reduce for the whole process, so two non-fused all-reduces move: the target model's last-layer all-reduce (it feeds the final norm, the logits and the draft's input hidden states) and the draft (MTP) layer's all-reduces. Up to 1,365 tokens they now use SGLang's custom all-reduce, which also accumulates in FP32. For 1,366–2,048-token prefill chunks they use NCCL, which SGLang runs with `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0` (Ring/Tree, BF16 rounding at each hop) instead of MNNVL with FP32 accumulation. The default backend already sends every chunk above 2,048 tokens through that same NCCL path. - The draft runs as shipped. The MTP layer never uses the CuTe DSL fusion (`install_cutedsl_fusion` returns `None` in speculative scope, and GLM-5.2's NextN layer skips it; the logs show 78 of 78 target layers fused on each rank), and `SGLANG_NVFP4_CKPT_FP8_NEXTN_MOE` is not set. - Outputs are not bitwise identical to the default backend, because rounding points and summation order differ.
## Speed Tests and Profiling **Which point, and why.** The low-latency end: GB300 NVFP4, aggregated TP4, c1 (the GLM-5.2 GB300 TP4 point of the Agentic Long-Context section). SGLang applies this fusion only to TP deployments without DP attention or a MoE all-to-all backend, so the high-throughput DP-attention points do not use it at all. At c1 a decode step usually carries one request with 5 draft tokens, so 5–15 tokens per all-reduce. Its gain most likely comes from faster small all-reduces (inferred: in the microbenchmark below, the CuTe DSL kernel takes 0.86–0.89× the time of `mnnvl` at 4–12 tokens). The same microbenchmark shows it slower at 16–20 and 96–256 tokens, which higher concurrency reaches (for example 4 or more requests with 5 draft tokens), so this PR recommends the flag only for c1. **Why an AgentX replay rather than a static workload.** TTFT depends on prefix-cache hits and on the sizes of the prefill chunks, and this flag's effect on TTFT depends on chunk size: the regression on the older build came from chunks above 2,048 tokens. In this trace 95.5% of prompt tokens were read from the prefix cache, and 2,049–8,192-token chunks were 203 of 290 prefill forwards and 94.5% of new prefill tokens (default arm; counts include the client's warm-up phase). A fixed-length random workload would not reproduce that mix. Decode time per token was measured in the same runs. **Setup (measured).** One GB300 node, 4 GPUs, image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20261026-8252e3af`, model `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`, the AgentX command for this point launched with `sglang.launch_server` (no Dynamo frontend), AgentX client 1.0.7 at c1, simulated MTP acceptance 3.33 (InferenceX's golden value). One node per run, fresh server per arm, 1,200 s windows, order: warm-up, default, `cutedsl`, default. Run 1 used the image's own SGLang; the replicate and the GPQA runs used a newer SGLang `main` tree laid over the same image, whose files on the flag's path are identical to the image's except for an opt-in row cap that was left unset (Builds, below).
Setup details, builds, launch and client commands - One GB300 node, 4 GPUs. Image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20261026-8252e3af` (`sha256:b4e4abb9e1dc038f7e14c85805be97e4f74abb46e541bd4edd31401d50a2e593`), FlashInfer 0.7.2, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. Model `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`. - **Builds.** Run 1 used the image's own SGLang (`8252e3af`). The replicate and both GPQA arms used the same image with SGLang's Python tree replaced by a newer `main` (`316ff4dce2`, 47 commits after `8252e3af`) plus one unmerged commit that adds an opt-in environment variable capping the rows the CuTe DSL fusion takes; the variable was unset in these runs, so behaviour is unchanged (code reading). On the flag's path, six files are identical in `316ff4dce2` and `8252e3af`: `layers/flashinfer_mnnvl_cutedsl.py`, `layers/flashinfer_comm_fusion.py`, `layers/layer_boundary/fusions/cutedsl.py`, `layers/layer_boundary/residual/add_norm.py`, `model_executor/runner/base_runner.py` and `distributed/bootstrap.py`; the unmerged commit adds the cap to five of them. `models/deepseek_v2.py`, where GLM-5.2 installs the fusion, differs between the two only by a `hasattr` → `is not None` change from #33250. - Client: AgentX agentic-coding trace replay (AgentX client 1.0.7), c1; requests carry `enable_thinking=true`, temperature 1 and top_p 0.95. - Each arm starts a fresh server and measures a 1,200 s window. Order on one node: a warm-up arm (default), then default, `cutedsl`, default. - MTP acceptance is simulated at 3.33, InferenceX's golden value for this model and draft length. - Differences from the AgentX command for this point: - `--flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend cutedsl` (the `cutedsl` arm only); - `sglang.launch_server` serves the client directly, instead of `dynamo.frontend` in front of `dynamo.sglang`. With one worker the frontend has no routing choice to make; that it adds only host-side request handling is an estimate, not measured; - 1,200 s windows instead of InferenceX's 3,600 s; AgentX client 1.0.7 (InferenceX's published run used 1.0.12); - image `nightly-dev-20261026-8252e3af` instead of the listed `nightly-dev-20261021-c1c287a4`, which predates #45565; - `NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1`, which InferenceX's GB300 workers also had from their environment (the recipe does not set it); - `--enable-metrics --enable-cache-report` (logging only) and the `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_*` variables, which InferenceX's harness also sets. - Every arm: exit code 0, no errors in the server log, identical KV-cache size (2,571,968 tokens), and mean accept length 3.332 / 3.332 / 3.335. Every 2,049–8,192-token prefill chunk ran in a CUDA graph (203 / 204 / 203, including warm-up). For this model the prefill graphs are "breakable": captured segments replay as graphs and the few operations that cannot be captured, such as sparse attention, run eagerly between them; the all-reduce sites are inside the captured segments. Default arms log `Auto-enabling FlashInfer AllReduce Fusion (auto) for GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` and `backend=mnnvl`. The `cutedsl` arm logs `Prepared the FlashInfer MNNVL CuTe DSL fusion workspace for M_max=8192 (78 fused layers)` on each of the 4 ranks and no `mnnvl` workspace. - The `cutedsl` arm also logs `MNNVL CuTe DSL: no shipped profile for tp=4 hidden=6144 top_k=8; re-targeting the GB300 presets at this shape ... benchmark against --flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend mnnvl before deploying a shape that matters.` This A/B is that benchmark. - The node also exported InfiniBand and socket NCCL settings, the same in every arm. Launch command (the `cutedsl` arm; the default arms omit the last line): ```bash NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 \ NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1 \ SGLANG_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=900 \ TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT=1800 \ SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.33 \ SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected \ SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 --served-model-name nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 \ --trust-remote-code --quantization modelopt_fp4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 --expert-parallel-size 1 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --bf16-gemm-backend cutedsl \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 8192 --context-length 1048576 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.83 --max-running-requests 8 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 8 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 4 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 5 \ --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-size 100 --hicache-write-policy write_back \ --hicache-io-backend direct --hicache-mem-layout page_first_direct \ --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 \ --weight-loader-prefetch-checkpoints \ --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load":true}' \ --watchdog-timeout 1800 --enable-metrics --enable-cache-report \ --flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend cutedsl ``` Client command (each arm): ```bash AIPERF_REQUIRED_SERVER_METRIC_PREFIX=sglang: \ AIPERF_HTTP_TCP_USER_TIMEOUT=900000 \ agentx profile --url http://127.0.0.1:30000 --model nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \ --tokenizer nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 --tokenizer-trust-remote-code \ --benchmark-duration 1200 --concurrency 1 \ --extra-inputs '{"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":true},"temperature":1,"top_p":0.95}' \ --warmup-grace-period 1800 --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126 ```
**Results, run 1 (measured; the image's own SGLang).** Each arm completed 149 requests; the 148 with at least 2 output tokens are paired by conversation and turn. Decode ms/token = (latency − TTFT) / (output tokens − 1). How each row compares `cutedsl` with the defaults: - decode, per-request ratio: the median over requests of `cutedsl` / default, pooled over both default arms (296 ratios); - percentile rows (decode p50 / p90, p90 interactivity, TTFT): the percentile of the 148 `cutedsl` requests against the same percentile of the 296 requests of both default arms taken together; - throughput: the whole window, against the mean of the two default arms. Intervals are 95% paired-bootstrap intervals that resample requests (2,000 draws; 10,000 for the per-request decode ratio, where each draw keeps both of a request's ratios). Noise = second default arm vs first. A change counts as beyond noise when it is larger than the noise and both `cutedsl`-vs-default pairs have the same sign. | Metric | default | `cutedsl` | default (repeat) | `cutedsl` vs defaults [95% CI] | Noise | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Decode ms/token, per-request ratio (median) | | | | **−3.45%** [−3.65, −3.18] | +0.04% | | Decode ms/token p50 | 2.964 | 2.857 | 2.965 | −3.62% [−4.08, −2.87] | +0.05% | | Decode ms/token p90 | 3.694 | 3.618 | 3.704 | −2.07% [−4.94, −1.24] | +0.28% | | p90 interactivity, 1000 / p90 ITL (tok/s per user) | 272.3 | 280.2 | 272.2 | +3.06% [+1.83, +5.74] | −0.03% | | TTFT p50 (ms) | 245 | 226 | 236 | −4.10% [−7.25, +1.97] | −3.98% | | TTFT p90 (ms) | 1,386 | 1,325 | 1,379 | **−3.94%** [−16.55, +4.43] | −0.52% | | TTFT p99 (ms) | 4,114 | 3,995 | 4,132 | −3.34% [−10.84, +0.32] | +0.44% | | Throughput, whole window (input + output tok/s/GPU) | 5,151 | 5,228 | 5,156 | +1.45% | +0.10% | - Decode: both pairs agree (−3.43% and −3.46% per request), far outside the +0.04% noise. - p90 TTFT: −3.94% [−16.55, +4.43]; both pairs are negative (−4.44% and −3.94%), beyond the 0.52% noise. The interval is wide because the p90 of 148 requests is set by the slowest 15 or so. - p50 TTFT: the −4.10% is about the size of the difference between the two default arms (−3.98%), so we claim only that p50 TTFT is not worse. - By prefill size (uncached prompt tokens), the per-request median TTFT change against the mean of the two default arms is negative in every bin, from −1.95% to −4.27%; above 8,192 new tokens it is −3.56%, with 0 of 28 requests slower. - For reference, InferenceX's published result for this point (image `nightly-dev-20261021-c1c287a4`, Dynamo frontend, 3,600 s, client 1.0.12) is 5,173 tok/s/GPU at 279.3 tok/s/user p90 interactivity; the default arms here measured 5,151 and 5,156 tok/s/GPU at 272.3 and 272.2 (shorter window, no Dynamo frontend, older client).
Replicate, run 2 (measured; newer main tree) Same image, flags, client and arm order, on another GB300 node, with the newer `main` tree described under Builds. 148 paired requests. - Decode ms/token, per-request ratio: −3.41% [−3.59, −3.16] (noise +0.03%). - p90 interactivity: +3.63% [+0.99, +11.80] (noise −0.05%). - TTFT p90: −4.63% [−16.22, −0.68] (noise −0.21%). - TTFT p50: −4.08% [−6.89, +2.97] (noise −3.89%, so again only "not worse"). - Throughput: 5,148 / 5,218 / 5,146 tok/s/GPU, +1.38% against the mean of the two default arms.
Run 3: memory check (measured; 900-s windows) Same image (its own SGLang), flags and arm order on a third GB300 node, with 900-s windows and no warm-up, to test the memory note below; 106 paired requests. Its perf numbers are reported but were not a decision input. - Decode ms/token, per-request ratio: −3.47% [−3.84, −2.99]. - TTFT p50: −5.02% (noise 0.32%). TTFT p90: +2.49% [−11.17, +67.82], within its noise (4.21%); the pairs disagree in sign (+3.17% and −1.00%). - Throughput: 5,691 / 5,824 / 5,691 tok/s/GPU (+2.3%).
An earlier run, excluded An earlier run on the same image was discarded: a shared-filesystem outage on the test cluster froze one default-backend arm for about 14 minutes. The server was waiting on a read from its Triton kernel cache, which sat on that filesystem; an unrelated process on the same node froze over the same interval, and both resumed when the storage recovered (attributed from timing and file-access records; no stack sample was taken). SGLang is not implicated. Over the 74 requests that arm completed, the run's valid default-vs-`cutedsl` pair agreed with the runs above (p50 decode time per token −3.24%).
**Counter-example on an older build (measured).** On `nightly-dev-20261016-a93f16f0` (which reports SGLang `c15edf31`, the image's build commit; FlashInfer 0.7.1), prefill CUDA graphs stopped at 2,048 tokens, so larger chunks ran eagerly. The same A/B (default / `cutedsl` / default, 1,200 s each, one node) gave decode −3.24% [−3.50, −3.03] (per-request ratio), but raised TTFT p50 from 274.7 ms to 299.5 ms (+9.0%; +9.6% over the paired requests). #45565 raised the MLA prefill CUDA-graph cap to min(8192, chunked-prefill size). With it, every 2,049–8,192-token chunk in runs 1 and 2 ran in a CUDA graph, and p50 TTFT no longer rises. The mechanism is not isolated: the two builds also differ in other commits (for example #43216, which changes NCCL graph registration) and in FlashInfer version.
All-reduce microbenchmark on GB300 (measured) One GB300 node, TP4, hidden size 6144, BF16, in the image under test with SGLang's own wrappers. Every arm runs in a CUDA graph; the time is the maximum over ranks, legs are interleaved, and the result is the median of leg medians. CuTe DSL all-reduce + residual + RMSNorm against the `mnnvl` fused kernel, with the CuTe DSL workspace sized for 256 tokens (at 256 tokens the 8,192-token workspace gives the same ratio, 1.08): | Tokens per call | 4 | 8 | 12 | 16 | 20 | 24–64 | 96 | 128 | 160 | 192 | 224 | 256 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | CuTe DSL / `mnnvl` time | 0.89 | 0.87 | 0.86 | 1.13 | 1.05 | 0.98–1.02 | 1.06 | 1.05 | 1.09 | 1.10 | 1.10 | 1.08 | With the 8,192-token workspace, CuTe DSL took 0.92–1.00× the time of `mnnvl` at 384–2,048 tokens, and 0.71–0.77× the time of NCCL + RMSNorm (what the default runs there) at 3,072–8,192 tokens.
GPU memory headroom (measured) - In each of the four `cutedsl` arms on this image (runs 1-3 and the excluded run), GPU memory in use while serving (nvidia-smi) settled about 8 GiB per GPU above the default arms: about 276.2 GiB against 268.2 GiB, out of 277.5 GiB. It then stayed flat for the rest of each window. - **It is PyTorch's cache.** In run 3, after each arm's window we paused the server and called `/continue_generation` with `torch_empty_cache`. PyTorch's reserved memory went from 271.8 to 231.3 GiB with the flag and from 263.0 to 231.3 GiB without it (each rank logs it), and nvidia-smi then read 235.7 GiB with the flag against 236.5 GiB for both default arms. So the extra 8 GiB was idle cache, which PyTorch reuses and frees when an allocation fails; at startup the flag uses about 0.8 GiB less. - What this does not show: whether the flag's peak working set during a forward is larger. Growth of the cache means only that the allocator once needed more segments, by peak or by fragmentation. - Allocations outside PyTorch cannot use that cache. While it is held, about 0.45 GiB is free, and each `cutedsl` arm logged 64 warnings when Triton kernels were first loaded during serving (16 loads of 8 distinct kernels on each of 4 ranks, most at the first moment two requests were running): `Triton kernel '...' device-loaded after serving started (free device mem: 0.45 GiB). Pre-load it during engine init to avoid CUDA OOM.` No default arm logged it (threshold 1 GiB). Every load and request succeeded. - The likely source of the cache (code reading, not tested): long-context prefills allocate large FP32 logits scratch blocks for the DSA indexer (GLM-5.2's sparse-attention token selector) in eager code, and which blocks the allocator keeps depends on the history of earlier allocations; the CuTe DSL workspace itself is about 267 MiB per rank. - Only `--mem-fraction-static 0.83` at c1 was tested with this flag. A lower fraction may not restore headroom, because the indexer's scratch budget during prefill graph replay is 0.2 × (1 − mem-fraction-static) × GPU memory (code reading), so the cache can grow into the freed memory too.

detail.body:
[by Claude Code] ## Motivation In every GLM-5.2 decoder layer, the attention output and the MLP output (an MoE in 75 of the 78 layers) are each summed across the tensor-parallel ranks (an all-reduce), added to the residual and normalized (RMSNorm). All-reduce fusion runs these three steps as one kernel. On one Blackwell node at TP4, SGLang turns it on by itself with `--flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend auto`, which resolves to FlashInfer's `mnnvl` backend (MNNVL is multi-node NVLink; these kernels exchange data over the NVLink fabric). That fusion covers batches of up to 2048 tokens; larger prefill chunks fall back to an NCCL all-reduce and a separate RMSNorm. The opt-in `cutedsl` backend uses FlashInfer kernels written in CuTe DSL (CUTLASS's Python kernel language) over the same fabric. It fuses batches up to `--max-prefill-tokens` (8192 in this deployment) and, for batches of up to 192 tokens, also folds in the MoE finalize (the weighted sum of the selected experts' outputs) and the shared-expert add. This PR adds a Configuration Tips bullet to the GLM-5.2 cookbook that recommends `cutedsl` for one deployment: GB300 NVFP4, aggregated TP4, concurrency 1 (c1), a point of the page's Agentic Long-Context section. That section lists commands measured with AgentX, SemiAnalysis InferenceX's agentic-coding benchmark, which replays recorded multi-turn coding-agent sessions against the server. The bullet gives the measured effect, the builds the flag needs (those with #45565, which raised the default prefill CUDA-graph size for MLA models from 2048 tokens to min(8192, chunked-prefill size)), the limit of the evidence to c1, and a memory note. Defaults and runtime code do not change; the default stays `auto` because only this one deployment was measured. The PR also corrects the server-arguments row for this flag, which does not list `cutedsl` and says `auto` picks `mnnvl` on SM90 (the code picks `trtllm`). Impact: - **Decode (measured):** time per output token about 3.4% lower in three runs: −3.45% [95% CI −3.65, −3.18] (default vs default +0.04%), −3.41% [−3.59, −3.16] in a replicate, and −3.47% [−3.84, −2.99] in a shorter third run. GLM-5.2 NVFP4, one GB300 node, TP4, c1, AgentX replay, 148 paired requests. - **TTFT (measured):** not worse. p90 −3.94% [95% CI −16.55, +4.43] and −4.63% [−16.22, −0.68] in the two 1,200-s runs, and +2.49% [−11.17, +67.82], within its noise, in the 900-s third run; p50 not worse in any run. - **Throughput (measured):** +1.45% input + output tokens/s per GPU against the mean of the two default arms (replicate +1.38%). - **Accuracy (measured):** GPQA-Diamond 0.9116 → 0.9003, −1.14 points [95% CI −2.78, +0.51], no significant change; MTP accept length 2.729 → 2.742. - **Scope (measured):** c1 only. In a GB300 microbenchmark over 4–256 tokens per call, the CuTe DSL kernel was faster than `mnnvl` only at 4–12 tokens, and 1.05–1.13× slower at 16–20 and 1.05–1.10× slower at 96–256 tokens, so the bullet tells readers to re-measure before raising concurrency. - **Builds without #45565 (measured):** on `nightly-dev-20261016-a93f16f0` the flag raised p50 TTFT by 9.0% (decode still −3.24%), so the bullet names a minimum build. - **Memory (measured):** with the flag, PyTorch's caching allocator held about 8 GiB more idle cache per GPU while serving at `--mem-fraction-static 0.83`, leaving 0.45 GiB free for allocations outside PyTorch; emptying the cache brought both backends to the same level (within 0.8 GiB). No request failed. ## Modifications **+3 / −2 docs (2 files); no runtime code, no tests.** Base: `main` at `f2d31889258d22214d9541e40b1e1e6961ce95e7`. - **GLM-5.2 Configuration Tips** (`docs/cookbook/autoregressive/GLM/GLM-5.2.mdx`): one new bullet. It says what the flag changes and where it was measured, gives the effect, names the build requirement (#45565; the image the Agentic Long-Context section lists for this point, `nightly-dev-20261021-c1c287a4`, predates it), the older-build counter-example, the c1-only scope with the microbenchmark caveat and the memory note, and says that the Deploy panel cells do not set the flag. The bullet names `nightly-dev-20261026-8252e3af` (measured) or newer; the first nightly built after #45565 merged, `nightly-dev-20261024-5994c559`, was not measured. - **Server-arguments row** (`docs/docs/advanced_features/server_arguments.mdx`, `--flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend`): the description follows the field's help string on `main` and adds facts read from the code: when SGLang turns the fusion on by itself (including the DeepSeek-V4.1 TP4 exception), the 2048-token limit of `trtllm` and `mnnvl`, and for `cutedsl` its TP sizes, forward modes and workspace bound, and that it turns the other fusion off for the whole process, so speculative draft layers run unfused. The options column gains `cutedsl`. The old row's "Defaults to auto" and "mnnvl on SM90" did not match the code (`auto` picks `trtllm` on SM90).
Where each fact in the row comes from (code on main) - Help string: `python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/fields/exec_.py`; the options match the field's `Literal`, and the default stays `None`. - Auto-enable: TP size above 1, no DP attention, no MoE all-to-all backend, multi-node only on Blackwell, and not for DeepSeek-V4.1 (hidden size 5120) at TP4 on one Blackwell node, which keeps its custom all-reduce (`_flashinfer_allreduce_fusion_auto_enable` and `prefer_custom_dsv41` in `arg_groups/overrides.py`). - `auto` resolves to `mnnvl` on Blackwell and `trtllm` on SM90 single-node (`_resolve_backend` in `layers/flashinfer_comm_fusion.py`). - The 2048-token limit of the `trtllm` and `mnnvl` fusion: `FUSE_ALLREDUCE_MAX_BATCH_SIZE` in `layers/layer_boundary/residual/add_norm.py`. - `cutedsl`: TP sizes 2, 4, 8 and 16 (`SUPPORTED_TP_SIZES` in `layers/flashinfer_mnnvl_cutedsl.py`); decode, extend and target-verify batches only (`_is_supported_forward_mode` in `layers/layer_boundary/fusions/cutedsl.py`); workspace bound, the largest of `--max-prefill-tokens`, `--max-running-requests`, the CUDA graph batch sizes and the decode graph batch size × draft tokens (`_resolve_max_m`, `cutedsl_moe_max_num_tokens`); the other fusion is off for the whole process (`uses_cutedsl_ar_fusion`), and draft layers never get the CuTe DSL fusion (`install_cutedsl_fusion` returns `None` in speculative scope), so they run unfused.
- **Not changed:** the AgentX panel data (`docs/src/snippets/agentx/zai-org/glm-5.2.jsx`) and the Deploy panel. Each AgentX entry mirrors an InferenceX submission and links to the run that measured it. The GB300 Agg TP4 entry's run used `nightly-dev-20261021-c1c287a4` (before #45565) without this flag, so editing that entry here would attach a command to a run that did not measure it. The flag can enter that entry through the regular AgentX sync once an InferenceX run with it exists. **Checks.** - [x] `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args_docs_coverage.py` (the CPU CI test for `server_arguments.mdx`): 4 of 4 pass with this row on a CPU checkout of `main` at `cb55d77d`, and a misspelled flag in the new row makes `test_no_stale_rows` fail, so the test does read the row. Since then, `main` has changed none of the code this row describes (`exec_.py`, `overrides.py` and the fusion files have no all-reduce-fusion changes up to the base commit); CI reruns the test on this base. - [x] The pre-commit hooks that apply to `.mdx` files: no trailing whitespace, final newlines present, no merge markers, `codespell` clean on the added lines. The full `pre-commit run` was not completed locally. - [ ] `mint validate` and `mint broken-links` in `docs/` ## Accuracy Tests **GPQA-Diamond (measured).** `sgl-eval` 0.1.3 (the version pinned in `python/pyproject.toml`): 198 questions × 4 repeats, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95 (the checkpoint's recommended sampling), max tokens 200,000, 32 client threads. Real MTP acceptance (no simulation). Server: the launch command under Speed Tests without the `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_*` variables, plus `--max-running-requests 32 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 32` so that the 32 threads run concurrently. The two arms differ only in the flag. Build: the replicate build described under Speed Tests (Builds). The two arms ran on different GB300 nodes on different days. | | default (`auto` → `mnnvl`) | `cutedsl` | |---|---|---| | GPQA-Diamond pass@1 (792 samples) | 0.9116 | 0.9003 | | Paired difference per question (bootstrap, 10,000 draws) | | −1.14 points, 95% CI [−2.78, +0.51] | | MTP accept length (server counters) | 2.7293 | 2.7420 (+0.47%) | | Truncated responses | 0.13% | 0.38% | | Mean completion tokens | 23,542 | 23,951 | The interval contains 0, so there is no significant change. At this sample size a drop of about 2.3 points is detectable with 80% power, so a loss of about 1 point cannot be excluded.
GPQA command and dataset ```bash sgl-eval run gpqa --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 --model nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \ --n-repeats 4 --num-threads 32 --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --max-tokens 200000 \ --chat-template-kwarg enable_thinking=true --from-dataset gpqa_diamond_public.jsonl ``` The Hugging Face GPQA set is gated, so both arms read the same local file: the 198 GPQA-Diamond questions from the public OpenAI simple-evals CSV, formatted with sgl-eval's own GPQA prompt formatting (seed 42) and passed with `--from-dataset`. Absolute scores may therefore differ slightly from runs on sgl-eval's own copy; the comparison is paired.
Precision (code reading of SGLang 8252e3af and FlashInfer 0.7.2, plus server logs) - No dtype or quantization change. The two CuTe DSL kernels SGLang calls (all-reduce + residual + RMSNorm, and MoE finalize + all-reduce + residual + RMSNorm) read and write BF16 and accumulate in FP32; neither has an FP8 or FP4 output. - One narrow change. In a `cutedsl` process SGLang turns off its older MNNVL all-reduce for the whole process, so two non-fused all-reduces move: the target model's last-layer all-reduce (it feeds the final norm, the logits and the draft's input hidden states) and the draft (MTP) layer's all-reduces. Up to 1,365 tokens they now use SGLang's custom all-reduce, which also accumulates in FP32. For 1,366–2,048-token prefill chunks they use NCCL, which SGLang runs with `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0` (Ring/Tree, BF16 rounding at each hop) instead of MNNVL with FP32 accumulation. The default backend already sends every chunk above 2,048 tokens through that same NCCL path. - The draft runs as shipped. The MTP layer never uses the CuTe DSL fusion (`install_cutedsl_fusion` returns `None` in speculative scope, and GLM-5.2's NextN layer skips it; the logs show 78 of 78 target layers fused on each rank), and `SGLANG_NVFP4_CKPT_FP8_NEXTN_MOE` is not set. - Outputs are not bitwise identical to the default backend, because rounding points and summation order differ.
## Speed Tests and Profiling **Which point, and why.** The low-latency end: GB300 NVFP4, aggregated TP4, c1 (the GLM-5.2 GB300 TP4 point of the Agentic Long-Context section). SGLang applies this fusion only to TP deployments without DP attention or a MoE all-to-all backend, so the high-throughput DP-attention points do not use it at all. At c1 a decode step usually carries one request with 5 draft tokens, so 5–15 tokens per all-reduce. Its gain most likely comes from faster small all-reduces (inferred: in the microbenchmark below, the CuTe DSL kernel takes 0.86–0.89× the time of `mnnvl` at 4–12 tokens). The same microbenchmark shows it slower at 16–20 and 96–256 tokens, which higher concurrency reaches (for example 4 or more requests with 5 draft tokens), so this PR recommends the flag only for c1. **Why an AgentX replay rather than a static workload.** TTFT depends on prefix-cache hits and on the sizes of the prefill chunks, and this flag's effect on TTFT depends on chunk size: the regression on the older build came from chunks above 2,048 tokens. In this trace 95.5% of prompt tokens were read from the prefix cache, and 2,049–8,192-token chunks were 203 of 290 prefill forwards and 94.5% of new prefill tokens (default arm; counts include the client's warm-up phase). A fixed-length random workload would not reproduce that mix. Decode time per token was measured in the same runs. **Setup (measured).** One GB300 node, 4 GPUs, image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20261026-8252e3af`, model `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`, the AgentX command for this point launched with `sglang.launch_server` (no Dynamo frontend), AgentX client 1.0.7 at c1, simulated MTP acceptance 3.33 (InferenceX's golden value). One node per run, fresh server per arm, 1,200 s windows, order: warm-up, default, `cutedsl`, default. Run 1 used the image's own SGLang; the replicate and the GPQA runs used a newer SGLang `main` tree laid over the same image, whose files on the flag's path are identical to the image's except for an opt-in row cap that was left unset (Builds, below).
Setup details, builds, launch and client commands - One GB300 node, 4 GPUs. Image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20261026-8252e3af` (`sha256:b4e4abb9e1dc038f7e14c85805be97e4f74abb46e541bd4edd31401d50a2e593`), FlashInfer 0.7.2, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. Model `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`. - **Builds.** Run 1 used the image's own SGLang (`8252e3af`). The replicate and both GPQA arms used the same image with SGLang's Python tree replaced by a newer `main` (`316ff4dce2`, 47 commits after `8252e3af`) plus one unmerged commit that adds an opt-in environment variable capping the rows the CuTe DSL fusion takes; the variable was unset in these runs, so behaviour is unchanged (code reading). On the flag's path, six files are identical in `316ff4dce2` and `8252e3af`: `layers/flashinfer_mnnvl_cutedsl.py`, `layers/flashinfer_comm_fusion.py`, `layers/layer_boundary/fusions/cutedsl.py`, `layers/layer_boundary/residual/add_norm.py`, `model_executor/runner/base_runner.py` and `distributed/bootstrap.py`; the unmerged commit adds the cap to five of them. `models/deepseek_v2.py`, where GLM-5.2 installs the fusion, differs between the two only by a `hasattr` → `is not None` change from #33250. - Client: AgentX agentic-coding trace replay (AgentX client 1.0.7), c1; requests carry `enable_thinking=true`, temperature 1 and top_p 0.95. - Each arm starts a fresh server and measures a 1,200 s window. Order on one node: a warm-up arm (default), then default, `cutedsl`, default. - MTP acceptance is simulated at 3.33, InferenceX's golden value for this model and draft length. - Differences from the AgentX command for this point: - `--flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend cutedsl` (the `cutedsl` arm only); - `sglang.launch_server` serves the client directly, instead of `dynamo.frontend` in front of `dynamo.sglang`. With one worker the frontend has no routing choice to make; that it adds only host-side request handling is an estimate, not measured; - 1,200 s windows instead of InferenceX's 3,600 s; AgentX client 1.0.7 (InferenceX's published run used 1.0.12); - image `nightly-dev-20261026-8252e3af` instead of the listed `nightly-dev-20261021-c1c287a4`, which predates #45565; - `NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1`, which InferenceX's GB300 workers also had from their environment (the recipe does not set it); - `--enable-metrics --enable-cache-report` (logging only) and the `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_*` variables, which InferenceX's harness also sets. - Every arm: exit code 0, no errors in the server log, identical KV-cache size (2,571,968 tokens), and mean accept length 3.332 / 3.332 / 3.335. Every 2,049–8,192-token prefill chunk ran in a CUDA graph (203 / 204 / 203, including warm-up). For this model the prefill graphs are "breakable": captured segments replay as graphs and the few operations that cannot be captured, such as sparse attention, run eagerly between them; the all-reduce sites are inside the captured segments. Default arms log `Auto-enabling FlashInfer AllReduce Fusion (auto) for GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` and `backend=mnnvl`. The `cutedsl` arm logs `Prepared the FlashInfer MNNVL CuTe DSL fusion workspace for M_max=8192 (78 fused layers)` on each of the 4 ranks and no `mnnvl` workspace. - The `cutedsl` arm also logs `MNNVL CuTe DSL: no shipped profile for tp=4 hidden=6144 top_k=8; re-targeting the GB300 presets at this shape ... benchmark against --flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend mnnvl before deploying a shape that matters.` This A/B is that benchmark. - The node also exported InfiniBand and socket NCCL settings, the same in every arm. Launch command (the `cutedsl` arm; the default arms omit the last line): ```bash NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 \ NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1 \ SGLANG_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=900 \ TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT=1800 \ SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.33 \ SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected \ SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 --served-model-name nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 \ --trust-remote-code --quantization modelopt_fp4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 --expert-parallel-size 1 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --bf16-gemm-backend cutedsl \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 8192 --context-length 1048576 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.83 --max-running-requests 8 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 8 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 4 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 5 \ --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-size 100 --hicache-write-policy write_back \ --hicache-io-backend direct --hicache-mem-layout page_first_direct \ --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 \ --weight-loader-prefetch-checkpoints \ --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load":true}' \ --watchdog-timeout 1800 --enable-metrics --enable-cache-report \ --flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend cutedsl ``` Client command (each arm): ```bash AIPERF_REQUIRED_SERVER_METRIC_PREFIX=sglang: \ AIPERF_HTTP_TCP_USER_TIMEOUT=900000 \ agentx profile --url http://127.0.0.1:30000 --model nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \ --tokenizer nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 --tokenizer-trust-remote-code \ --benchmark-duration 1200 --concurrency 1 \ --extra-inputs '{"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":true},"temperature":1,"top_p":0.95}' \ --warmup-grace-period 1800 --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126 ```
**Results, run 1 (measured; the image's own SGLang).** Each arm completed 149 requests; the 148 with at least 2 output tokens are paired by conversation and turn. Decode ms/token = (latency − TTFT) / (output tokens − 1). How each row compares `cutedsl` with the defaults: - decode, per-request ratio: the median over requests of `cutedsl` / default, pooled over both default arms (296 ratios); - percentile rows (decode p50 / p90, p90 interactivity, TTFT): the percentile of the 148 `cutedsl` requests against the same percentile of the 296 requests of both default arms taken together; - throughput: the whole window, against the mean of the two default arms. Intervals are 95% paired-bootstrap intervals that resample requests (2,000 draws; 10,000 for the per-request decode ratio, where each draw keeps both of a request's ratios). Noise = second default arm vs first. A change counts as beyond noise when it is larger than the noise and both `cutedsl`-vs-default pairs have the same sign. | Metric | default | `cutedsl` | default (repeat) | `cutedsl` vs defaults [95% CI] | Noise | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Decode ms/token, per-request ratio (median) | | | | **−3.45%** [−3.65, −3.18] | +0.04% | | Decode ms/token p50 | 2.964 | 2.857 | 2.965 | −3.62% [−4.08, −2.87] | +0.05% | | Decode ms/token p90 | 3.694 | 3.618 | 3.704 | −2.07% [−4.94, −1.24] | +0.28% | | p90 interactivity, 1000 / p90 ITL (tok/s per user) | 272.3 | 280.2 | 272.2 | +3.06% [+1.83, +5.74] | −0.03% | | TTFT p50 (ms) | 245 | 226 | 236 | −4.10% [−7.25, +1.97] | −3.98% | | TTFT p90 (ms) | 1,386 | 1,325 | 1,379 | **−3.94%** [−16.55, +4.43] | −0.52% | | TTFT p99 (ms) | 4,114 | 3,995 | 4,132 | −3.34% [−10.84, +0.32] | +0.44% | | Throughput, whole window (input + output tok/s/GPU) | 5,151 | 5,228 | 5,156 | +1.45% | +0.10% | - Decode: both pairs agree (−3.43% and −3.46% per request), far outside the +0.04% noise. - p90 TTFT: −3.94% [−16.55, +4.43]; both pairs are negative (−4.44% and −3.94%), beyond the 0.52% noise. The interval is wide because the p90 of 148 requests is set by the slowest 15 or so. - p50 TTFT: the −4.10% is about the size of the difference between the two default arms (−3.98%), so we claim only that p50 TTFT is not worse. - By prefill size (uncached prompt tokens), the per-request median TTFT change against the mean of the two default arms is negative in every bin, from −1.95% to −4.27%; above 8,192 new tokens it is −3.56%, with 0 of 28 requests slower. - For reference, InferenceX's published result for this point (image `nightly-dev-20261021-c1c287a4`, Dynamo frontend, 3,600 s, client 1.0.12) is 5,173 tok/s/GPU at 279.3 tok/s/user p90 interactivity; the default arms here measured 5,151 and 5,156 tok/s/GPU at 272.3 and 272.2 (shorter window, no Dynamo frontend, older client).
Replicate, run 2 (measured; newer main tree) Same image, flags, client and arm order, on another GB300 node, with the newer `main` tree described under Builds. 148 paired requests. - Decode ms/token, per-request ratio: −3.41% [−3.59, −3.16] (noise +0.03%). - p90 interactivity: +3.63% [+0.99, +11.80] (noise −0.05%). - TTFT p90: −4.63% [−16.22, −0.68] (noise −0.21%). - TTFT p50: −4.08% [−6.89, +2.97] (noise −3.89%, so again only "not worse"). - Throughput: 5,148 / 5,218 / 5,146 tok/s/GPU, +1.38% against the mean of the two default arms.
Run 3: memory check (measured; 900-s windows) Same image (its own SGLang), flags and arm order on a third GB300 node, with 900-s windows and no warm-up, to test the memory note below; 106 paired requests. Its perf numbers are reported but were not a decision input. - Decode ms/token, per-request ratio: −3.47% [−3.84, −2.99]. - TTFT p50: −5.02% (noise 0.32%). TTFT p90: +2.49% [−11.17, +67.82], within its noise (4.21%); the pairs disagree in sign (+3.17% and −1.00%). - Throughput: 5,691 / 5,824 / 5,691 tok/s/GPU (+2.3%).
An earlier run, excluded An earlier run on the same image was discarded: a shared-filesystem outage on the test cluster froze one default-backend arm for about 14 minutes. The server was waiting on a read from its Triton kernel cache, which sat on that filesystem; an unrelated process on the same node froze over the same interval, and both resumed when the storage recovered (attributed from timing and file-access records; no stack sample was taken). SGLang is not implicated. Over the 74 requests that arm completed, the run's valid default-vs-`cutedsl` pair agreed with the runs above (p50 decode time per token −3.24%).
**Counter-example on an older build (measured).** On `nightly-dev-20261016-a93f16f0` (which reports SGLang `c15edf31`, the image's build commit; FlashInfer 0.7.1), prefill CUDA graphs stopped at 2,048 tokens, so larger chunks ran eagerly. The same A/B (default / `cutedsl` / default, 1,200 s each, one node) gave decode −3.24% [−3.50, −3.03] (per-request ratio), but raised TTFT p50 from 274.7 ms to 299.5 ms (+9.0%; +9.6% over the paired requests). #45565 raised the MLA prefill CUDA-graph cap to min(8192, chunked-prefill size). With it, every 2,049–8,192-token chunk in runs 1 and 2 ran in a CUDA graph, and p50 TTFT no longer rises. The mechanism is not isolated: the two builds also differ in other commits (for example #43216, which changes NCCL graph registration) and in FlashInfer version.
All-reduce microbenchmark on GB300 (measured) One GB300 node, TP4, hidden size 6144, BF16, in the image under test with SGLang's own wrappers. Every arm runs in a CUDA graph; the time is the maximum over ranks, legs are interleaved, and the result is the median of leg medians. CuTe DSL all-reduce + residual + RMSNorm against the `mnnvl` fused kernel, with the CuTe DSL workspace sized for 256 tokens (at 256 tokens the 8,192-token workspace gives the same ratio, 1.08): | Tokens per call | 4 | 8 | 12 | 16 | 20 | 24–64 | 96 | 128 | 160 | 192 | 224 | 256 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | CuTe DSL / `mnnvl` time | 0.89 | 0.87 | 0.86 | 1.13 | 1.05 | 0.98–1.02 | 1.06 | 1.05 | 1.09 | 1.10 | 1.10 | 1.08 | With the 8,192-token workspace, CuTe DSL took 0.92–1.00× the time of `mnnvl` at 384–2,048 tokens, and 0.71–0.77× the time of NCCL + RMSNorm (what the default runs there) at 3,072–8,192 tokens.
GPU memory headroom (measured) - In each of the four `cutedsl` arms on this image (runs 1-3 and the excluded run), GPU memory in use while serving (nvidia-smi) settled about 8 GiB per GPU above the default arms: about 276.2 GiB against 268.2 GiB, out of 277.5 GiB. It then stayed flat for the rest of each window. - **It is PyTorch's cache.** In run 3, after each arm's window we paused the server and called `/continue_generation` with `torch_empty_cache`. PyTorch's reserved memory went from 271.8 to 231.3 GiB with the flag and from 263.0 to 231.3 GiB without it (each rank logs it), and nvidia-smi then read 235.7 GiB with the flag against 236.5 GiB for both default arms. So the extra 8 GiB was idle cache, which PyTorch reuses and frees when an allocation fails; at startup the flag uses about 0.8 GiB less. - What this does not show: whether the flag's peak working set during a forward is larger. Growth of the cache means only that the allocator once needed more segments, by peak or by fragmentation. - Allocations outside PyTorch cannot use that cache. While it is held, about 0.45 GiB is free, and each `cutedsl` arm logged 64 warnings when Triton kernels were first loaded during serving (16 loads of 8 distinct kernels on each of 4 ranks, most at the first moment two requests were running): `Triton kernel '...' device-loaded after serving started (free device mem: 0.45 GiB). Pre-load it during engine init to avoid CUDA OOM.` No default arm logged it (threshold 1 GiB). Every load and request succeeded. - The likely source of the cache (code reading, not tested): long-context prefills allocate large FP32 logits scratch blocks for the DSA indexer (GLM-5.2's sparse-attention token selector) in eager code, and which blocks the allocator keeps depends on the history of earlier allocations; the CuTe DSL workspace itself is about 267 MiB per rank. - Only `--mem-fraction-static 0.83` at c1 was tested with this flag. A lower fraction may not restore headroom, because the indexer's scratch budget during prefill graph replay is 0.2 × (1 − mem-fraction-static) × GPU memory (code reading), so the cache can grow into the freed memory too.

@@ -178,6 +178,7 @@ import { agentx } from "/src/snippets/agentx/zai-org/glm-5.2.jsx";
 - **BF16 weights need more GPUs.** The full-precision build (`zai-org/GLM-5.2`, ~1.5 TB) does not fit a single 8×H200 / 8×B200 / 4×GB300 node. It fits single-node on **8×B300** (TP8, ~2.1 TB HBM) — **verified**; on the smaller GPUs it needs a **multi-node** layout (e.g. 2×8×H200 or 2×8×B200 at TP16, 2×4×GB300 at TP8), and those **multi-node BF16 recipes are still proposed/inferred** (`verified: false`). FP8 is the recommended deployment. Use the same DSA / MTP / chunked-prefill guidance as FP8. On B300, BF16 low-latency matches FP8 (the sm103 FP8 path is not yet optimized), but FP8 wins at the balanced/high-throughput points.
 - **PD Disaggregation (prefill/decode).** GLM-5.2 is a DSA model and runs under prefill/decode disaggregation — toggle the **PD Disagg** card in the [Playground above](#playground) (pick a Prefill/Decode role + transfer backend, then front the roles with `sglang_router.launch_router --pd-disaggregation`). The Mooncake backend **auto-detects the InfiniBand HCA**, so no device flag is needed by default; only add `--disaggregation-ib-device mlx5_0` (your NIC) if auto-detection picks the wrong device or KV transfer fails to connect. On H200 Docker, expose the IB HCAs to the container (`--privileged --ulimit memlock=-1`, or `--device /dev/infiniband:/dev/infiniband --cap-add IPC_LOCK`) — without IB exposure Mooncake silently falls back to TCP.
 - **Chunked-prefill size is regime-dependent.** At long input (8K+) the default `--chunked-prefill-size 2048` is too small and leaves the balanced point prefill-bound (queueing dominates TTFT). Raising it to `--chunked-prefill-size 32768` on the balanced recipe gave roughly **+34–78% output throughput and −39–59% TTFT** on 8×H200 and 8×B200 (8K-in / 1K-out) in our testing. It is **neutral for high-throughput** (decode-bound there) — keep the default. `--max-running-requests` tracks KV capacity, not a tuning free-for-all: ~60–90 concurrent 8K+1K FP8 requests fit on a single 8-GPU node, so pin balanced near `--max-running-requests 80` and let high-throughput run wider.
+- **GB300 NVFP4, TP4, concurrency 1: add `--flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend cutedsl`.** It moves the fused all-reduce + residual add + RMSNorm from the default FlashInfer `mnnvl` kernels, which stop at 2048 tokens, to FlashInfer's CuTe DSL kernels, which also fuse larger prefill chunks. Added to the GB300 NVFP4 Agg TP4 concurrency-1 command in the [Agentic Long-Context section](#agentic-long-context-deployment), it lowered decode time per output token by about 3.4% in three runs without making TTFT worse, and did not significantly change GPQA-Diamond. It needs a build with [#45565](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45565), such as `nightly-dev-20261026-8252e3af` (tested) or newer; the image that section lists for this point, `nightly-dev-20261021-c1c287a4`, is older. On the older `nightly-dev-20261016-a93f16f0`, the flag raised p50 TTFT by about 9%. Re-measure before raising concurrency: in a microbenchmark the CuTe DSL kernel was slower than `mnnvl` at 16–20 and 96–256 tokens per call. With the flag, PyTorch kept about 8 GiB more cached memory per GPU while serving, leaving 0.45 GiB free for allocations outside PyTorch; only `--mem-fraction-static 0.83` was tested. The Deploy panel cells do not set this flag.
 
 - **AMD GPUs (MI300X / MI325X / MI355X).** FP8 (`zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8`) runs single-node at `tp=8` on all three. BF16 (`zai-org/GLM-5.2`, ~1.51 TB) only fits single-node on **MI325X** (2 TB HBM) and **MI355X** (2.3 TB); **MI300X** (1.5 TB) cannot hold the BF16 weights plus KV cache on one node, so use FP8 there (or a multi-node BF16 layout once validated). Use the DSA tilelang backend (`--dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang`) and add `--chunked-prefill-size 131072` plus `--watchdog-timeout 1200` (20 min for weight loading). FP8 uses about half the memory of BF16 (~89 GB/GPU vs ~175 GB/GPU). GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V3.2 share the same model structure; for other DSA / HiSparse tips see the [DeepSeek-V3.2 cookbook](../DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V3_2).
 - **MI355X MXFP4 (gfx950-only).** AMD publishes a Quark-quantized **`amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4`** build for MI355X. It needs `--trust-remote-code` (Quark's custom quant config) and runs at `tp=4` (the 4-bit MoE weights fit a 4-GPU slice) with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, the DSA triton backends (`--dsa-prefill-backend triton --dsa-decode-backend triton`, also SGLang's ROCm default), and the same `--chunked-prefill-size` and `--watchdog-timeout` as the FP8/BF16 recipes above. At `tp=4` this shape — 16 query heads per rank on an FP8 KV cache — is the one the gfx950 sparse-MLA kernels are tuned for; the `tp=8` recipes above stay on tilelang, which is what their published numbers were measured with. This recipe is carried over from the validated `amd/GLM-5.1-MXFP4` MI355X deployment (same DSA architecture family) and has not yet been benchmarked on GLM-5.2, so the Deploy panel marks it unverified.
